source: IL 2019 diagnosis 2026-07-18 (cor 1.00 of clean state-AGI gap with state_ref before the fix)

expected_magnitude: zero at the state level

description: PolicyEngine nets the one-time 2021 IL individual income tax rebate ($50/filer + $100/dependent, paid 2022) into 2021 state_income_tax; one-time rebates are outside our v1 state liability concept. 2022-2024 IL cells validate at 99.2-99.5% clean
expected_magnitude: $50-$400 per household, round amounts
source: PE matrix diagnosis 2026-07-18 (95 clean mismatches all +$100/$200/$400)

PE's pre-refund co_income_tax_before_refundable_credits matches our calculator exactly on hand cases
expected_magnitude: $153-$1,600 per return, point masses at tier values
source: CO dive 2026-07-18 (81% of 2023 clean mismatches at exactly +800/+1600)

description: TAXSIM does not model the OH Business Income Deduction (IT BUS, R.C. 5747.01(A)(31)): first $250k/$125k-MFS of business income is deducted and the excess taxed at a flat 3%, while TAXSIM taxes business income at regular schedule rates; excluded via predicate on records claiming the BID
expected_magnitude: deduction times marginal rate plus (rate - 3%) on the excess; large for pass-through owners
source: OH 2019 diagnosis 2026-07-19 (74% of fed-aligned mismatches have st_bid > 0; 57% show v32 - st_agi exactly equal to BID; 97.5% of BID-record diffs negative)

description: Residual +$650 point-mass cluster (~150/yr): TAXSIM grants the OH Joint Filing Credit (5-20% capped $650) on returns where our earned-income proxy for each spouse's $500 qualifying-income test denies it; suspected mechanism is qualifying income beyond earnings (documented proxy limitation in the OH tracker row)

description: TAXSIM's PA base appears to net losses across income classes (median our st_agi minus v32 = +$10k among mismatches; 84% of mismatches positive, mean +$7.8k) where PA law bars cross-class and spousal offsets, flooring each class at zero; our within-unit class netting is itself a documented approximation. Note TAXSIM DOES model Tax Forgiveness (verified: 86% of forgiveness records match raw; back-adding the credit drops match to 14%)
expected_magnitude: loss amounts times 3.07%, concentrated in loss-heavy records

description: Permanent Building Fund filing-edge: symmetric +/-$10 point masses (~810 records each side in 2019) — both models levy the $10 PBF but with different required-to-file conditions (ours: federal-filer flag with blind exemption; TAXSIM's apparently income-threshold based)
expected_magnitude: exactly $10

description: CTC eligibility cluster: -$205 point mass (~75/yr) where we grant the $205-per-child credit (dep ages 0-16 via dep_age slots) and TAXSIM does not; suspected dependent-age concept difference
expected_magnitude: $205 per affected child

description: Itemizer deduction-rebuild divergence: TAXSIM's state itemized (v35) runs a median $21.8k BELOW our (item_ded - line-14 addback) and TAXSIM flips 36% of our itemizers to the standard deduction -- consistent with TAXSIM removing its full computed state income tax (SALT circularity) instead of the Form 40 line 14 capped property-first-fill formula (our encoding matches the published worksheet, test ID-3). Liability diff = bracket rate x taxable wedge exactly (cor 1.000); non-itemizers agree (84.5% wedge=0), confirming the base machinery
expected_magnitude: large on high-income itemizers (p90 abs diff ~$33k)

description: 2017 SALT addback size: our line 14 addback = reported income/sales-tax component capped at itemized-over-standard (form rule, pre-cap era); TAXSIM removes a smaller amount from its itemized rebuild (its computed state tax; possibly Pease-prorated) -- item wedge cor -0.745 with the SALT income component, median our-effective-itemized $8.3k below v35, p10 -$95k. Direction: ours over. Non-itemizers agree (93.6% wedge=0); exemptions and std amounts match exactly (v33 vs pe_ded mean gap $1.5)
expected_magnitude: scales with reported state income tax; largest for high earners

description: QBID subset: ~10% of QBID non-itemizers show taxable wedge exactly -qbi_ded (TAXSIM QBID = 0 where ours > 0; suspected wage/SSTB-limit divergence). TAXSIM otherwise includes QBID (median QBID non-itemizer wedge/qbid ratio 0.035) -- the earlier omits-QBID hypothesis is refuted
expected_magnitude: 5.8-6.925% x QBID on the affected subset

description: Dependent-care deduction cap: care-expense records are 3.6x over-represented among residual non-itemizer mismatches with median wedge +$1.8k (ours higher = we deduct less); TAXSIM appears to allow more than the Form 39R worksheet caps ($3,000/$6,000, all years) -- possibly the statutory-$12,000 reading of 63-3022D that appears on no published worksheet (see id_research_core.md sec 5)
expected_magnitude: rate x (excess expenses over 3k/6k caps)
